messages:
maya: Quick sync: pilot plan for finer-grained auth routing. Goal: split routing + quota attribution for org keys, project keys, and service-account tokens without changing token format. Need agreement on policy order, telemetry tags, cache behavior, and console preview UX.

oleg: Nice. Are we adding any claims to tokens or relying on existing fields from auth-exchange? :eyes: 

maya: Relying on existing claims. We'll use `origin` (org/project) and `actor_type` (user/sa). Policy maps: project claim -> project route; actor_type=sa -> resolve SA binding; else org route.

jamie: Note: billing/quotas still key off `project_id` today. If routing flips to org for some tokens, we must have a safe fallback so customers don't see sudden quota moves.

maya: Plan: routing precedence: (1) explicit project_id claim; (2) resource_owner_project claim (for SA requests); (3) org fallback. Any unresolved requests get `project:unknown` in telemetry.

tanmay: Canary idea: mirror-only mode first (no enforcement). Emit a mirrored decision per request into a new telemetry stream and expose that in console as a "preview" for admins. Keep enforcement off until owners sign off.

oleg: Good. One more ops concern: our CDN/gateway caches responses keyed by token fingerprint. If route changes but token stays same we'll misattribute cached responses.

maya: For mirror mode we won't alter cache keys. When we enable enforcement we'll add `route-v{N}` into the cache key so we can roll cache semantics alongside routing. We'll also add short TTLs for the first canary.

jamie: Dashboards: create these panels: route_mix_by_origin, fallback_rate(project_unknown), projected_quota_shift. Also an alert if >3% of traffic would switch quota bucket compared to baseline.

maya: Example query for route drift: 
```sql
select mirror_route, actual_route, count(1) as cnt
from requests
where ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
group by 1,2;
```
We write mirror_route in middleware.

tanmay: Console UX: on the API Keys page show a small preview card "Would route to: project:proj-xx (why: explicit project_id)" with a toggle to run preview on live tokens. Opt-out default. Also allow exporting mismatches for owners.

oleg: Edge-case: SAs with cross-project roles. Which project gets quota? Request-level `resource_owner_project` wins; otherwise owner_project wins and we flag multi_project=true in telemetry.

maya: We'll also emit `route_sample_id` to each mirrored event so we can pull exact request traces into test infra for replay.

jamie: Headers for mirror mode (sample):
```
X-Route-Mirror: project:proj-42
X-Route-Observed: org:org-7
X-Route-Note: resolved-via-owner-fallback
```

tanmay: Rollout timeline suggestion:
- Day 0: deploy mirror middleware behind feature flag (0.5% traffic)
- Day 3: increase mirror to 10% and enable console preview for org admins
- Day 7: full mirror (100%) + dashboards enabled + owner notifications
- Day 14: enforcement canary (10%) with `route-v2` cache key and short TTLs
- Day 21+: ramp enforcement if metrics stable

oleg: Who owns which alerts? Eng-platform -> route-drift alerts; Billing infra -> quota-regression alerts; Product infra -> console preview bugs.

maya: I'll file tickets and assign owners. We'll add a runbook for quota regressions.

infra-bot: Deploy plan queued: auth-routing-service feature `mirror_routes=true` -> canary cluster A (enabled 0.5%) scheduled 2026-05-12T09:00:00Z

jamie: One catch: we should track the % of requests using fallback paths vs explicit mapping and set a remediation threshold. I'll add that to the dashboard.

maya: Action items:
- maya: PR with dashboard panels + alert rules (today)
- oleg: implement cache-key toggle and short-ttl behavior (this sprint)
- tanmay: console preview UI + export mismatches (this sprint)
- jamie: define quotas regression thresholds + runbook (this sprint)

maya: Thanks team. We'll iterate on the first mirror run and re-evaluate before enforcement. :rocket:
